items.title: Section: What Has Form Unfolds into Five Kinds, Closing the Two Worldly Dharmas

items.zh: 色有五種。一、諸大種，二、大種所造，三、有見有對，四、無見有對，五、無見無對。復次，有五無明。一、義愚，二、見愚，三、放逸愚，四、真實義愚，五、增上慢愚。
items.en: Form has five kinds: the primary elements, and what is derived from the primary elements, distinguished further into what has visible appearance and resistance, what is invisible yet has resistance, and what is invisible and free of resistance. Furthermore, there are five kinds of ignorance: ignorance regarding meaning, regarding view, of heedlessness, regarding the truth, and of overweening pride.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Craving for Existence, Read Two Different Ways

items.zh: 復次，有五種有愛。一、法性愛，二、誓願愛，三、愚癡愛，四、厭離愛，五、思擇愛。
items.en: Furthermore, there are five kinds of craving for existence: craving rooted in the nature of things, craving rooted in a vow, craving rooted in delusion, craving rooted in weariness, and craving rooted in careful reflection.

items.title: Section: Five Marks Establish Shamelessness, Their Reversal Establishes a Genuine Conscience

items.zh: 復次，由五種相，當知建立無慚無愧。一、於染污現行無有羞恥；二、於善不現行無有羞恥；三、於捨法受無有羞恥；四、親近惡友無有羞恥；五、於所作不能成辦無有羞恥。當知與此五相相違五種妙相，建立慚愧。
items.en: Furthermore, by five marks, one should know that shamelessness and lack of conscience are established: no shame when defiled states manifest; no shame when wholesome states fail to manifest; no shame in casting off one's precepts; no shame in drawing close to bad friends; no shame in accomplishing nothing at all. One should know that the five excellent marks reversing these establish a genuine shame and conscience.

items.title: Section: Five Marks of a Bad Teacher, Five Marks of a Bad Friend

items.zh: 復次，由五種相，當知建立惡說者性。一、無行故；二、邪行故；三、不忍故；四、無羞恥故；五、不律儀故。由五種相，建立惡友。一、無羞恥，二、有邪見，三、有懈怠，四、有邪行，五、性怯劣。當知與此五相相違五種妙相，立善說者及與善友。
items.en: Furthermore, by five marks, one should know that the nature of a bad speaker of the Dharma is established: absence of right conduct, presence of wrong conduct, lack of conviction, absence of shame, and lack of discipline. By five marks, a bad friend is established: absence of shame, presence of wrong views, laziness, wrongful conduct, and a base and cowardly disposition. One should know that the five excellent marks reversing these establish a good speaker of the Dharma and a good friend.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Calm-Abiding, Five Kinds of Insight

items.zh: 復次，由五種相立奢摩他。一、近分定所攝世間奢摩他，二、根本色定所攝世間奢摩他，三、根本無色定所攝世間奢摩他，四、聲聞、獨覺作意所攝出世奢摩他，五、菩薩作意所攝出世奢摩他。復次，由五種相，當知建立毘鉢舍那。一、盡所有性毘鉢舍那，二、如所有性毘鉢舍那，三、有相毘鉢舍那，四、思求毘鉢舍那，五、觀察毘鉢舍那。
items.en: Furthermore, by five marks, calm-abiding is established: mundane calm-abiding belonging to approach concentration, mundane calm-abiding belonging to the root form-realm absorptions, mundane calm-abiding belonging to the root formless-realm absorptions, transcendent calm-abiding belonging to the śrāvaka's and pratyekabuddha's mental engagement, and transcendent calm-abiding belonging to the bodhisattva's mental engagement. Furthermore, by five marks, one should know that insight is established: insight into the exhaustive nature of things, insight into things as they truly are, insight bearing a mental image, insight through reflective inquiry, and insight through detailed observation.

items.title: Section: Three Outflows — Desire, Existence, and Ignorance

items.zh: 復次，略由五相，建立欲漏。一、不定地事生隨眠故；二、隨順惡行故；三、善相違故；四、耽著諸欲故；五、能生壞苦、苦苦果故。彼諸煩惱，說名欲漏。略由五相，建立有漏。一、能生劣界諸煩惱，二、能生中界諸煩惱，三、能生妙界諸煩惱，四、能生無欲樂有諸煩惱，五、能生有欲樂有諸煩惱。
items.en: Furthermore, briefly, by five marks, the outflow of desire is established: producing latent tendencies through things of the unconcentrated ground (the desire realm), according with unwholesome conduct, opposing the wholesome, indulging in desires, and giving rise to the fruit of the suffering of change and of suffering itself. Those afflictions are called the outflow of desire. Briefly, by five marks, the outflow of existence is established: producing the afflictions leading to the inferior realm, to the middling realm, to the sublime realm, to craving non-existence, and to craving further existence.

items.title: Section: The Outflow of Ignorance and the Sixty-Two Wrong Views

items.zh: 略由五相，立邪解脫欲無明漏。一、有想論者，由有想論門生起無明；二、無想論者，由無想論門生起無明；三、非有想非無想論者，由非有想非無想論門生起無明；四、斷見論者，由斷見論門生起無明；五、現法涅槃論者，由現法涅槃論門生起無明。
items.en: Briefly, by five marks, the outflow of ignorance arising from a mistaken wish for liberation is established: proponents of a having-perception view give rise to ignorance through that very view; proponents of a no-perception view give rise to ignorance through that view; proponents of a neither-perceiving-nor-non-perceiving view give rise to ignorance through that view; proponents of annihilationism give rise to ignorance through that view; and proponents of a present-life-nirvana view give rise to ignorance through that view.

items.title: Section: Closing the Science of Inner Knowledge, Opening the Science of Logic

items.zh: 復次，略由五相，應知諸法差別道理。一、由相故；二、由體故；三、由業故；四、由法故；五、由因果故。
items.en: Furthermore, briefly, by five marks, one should know the reasoning behind the distinctions among dharmas: by characteristic, by substance, by function, by dharma, and by cause and result.

items.zh: 相者，謂由所依故，及行、住故。體者，謂由自體相故，及差別相故。業者，謂由自作用故，及邪、正行故。法者，謂由染、淨故，及世俗、勝義諦故。因果者，謂由近、遠故，及愛非愛故。

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Ultimate Treatise — by Hearing, by Disputation, by Right Practice

items.zh: 復次，有三種論。一、聽聞究竟論，二、諍訟究竟論，三、正行究竟論。聽聞究竟論者，謂婆羅門諸惡呪術。諍訟究竟論者，謂諸外道因明論。正行究竟論者，謂佛聖教。
items.en: Furthermore, there are three kinds of treatise: the ultimate treatise of hearing, the ultimate treatise of disputation, and the ultimate treatise of right practice. The ultimate treatise of hearing refers to the various harmful incantations of the brāhmaṇas. The ultimate treatise of disputation refers to the logical treatises of the non-Buddhist schools. The ultimate treatise of right practice refers to the Buddha's noble teaching.

items.zh: 復有三論。一、無義論，二、邪義論，三、第一義論。此三如前，隨其所應。復有三論。一、矯詐論，二、虛偽論，三、出離苦果論。如是三論，應知如前，隨其所應。

items.title: Section: Before Composing Any Treatise, Bow to Two Teachers and Hold Six Motivations

items.zh: 復次，若欲造論，當先歸禮二所敬師，方可造論。恭敬法故，先應歸禮論本大師；恭敬義故，復應歸禮開闡義師。欲造論者，要具六因，乃應造論。一、欲令法義當廣流布；二、欲令種種信解有情，由此因緣，隨一當能入正法故；三、為令失沒種種義門，重開顯故；四、為欲略攝廣散義故；五、為欲顯發甚深義故；六、欲以種種美妙言辭莊嚴法義，生淨信故。
items.en: Furthermore, if one wishes to compose a treatise, one should first bow in homage to the two revered teachers before one may compose. Out of reverence for the Dharma, one should first bow to the root teacher of the treatise; out of reverence for the meaning, one should further bow to the teacher who opens up and clarifies the meaning. One who wishes to compose a treatise must hold six motivations before one may compose: that the teaching and its meaning may circulate widely; that beings of various faith and understanding may, through this cause, enter the true Dharma; that meanings lost and fallen into obscurity may be reopened; that broadly scattered meaning may be condensed; that profound meaning may be revealed; and that the Dharma's meaning may be adorned with beautiful words so as to give rise to pure faith.

blocks.text: The inner science closes with short lists, and the science of logic (hetuvidyā) begins with how and why to write a treatise.
The treatise lists five kinds of form outright: the elements, what they produce, and the three pairs of visibility and resistance.
The fourth and fifth kinds are transcendent, for śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and for bodhisattvas.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the unconcentrated ground is the desire realm, with its five sense objects. The outflow of ignorance includes a mistaken wish for liberation, rooted in clinging to a self.

(Untranslated, 0657c26: marks, substance, function, dharma, and cause-and-effect as the topics.) Before writing a treatise, one bows to two teachers and holds six motivations; scattered meanings are gathered together. (Untranslated, 0658a05: treatises without meaning, with wrong meaning, and on the highest meaning; deceptive, false, and those leading out of suffering.)
Before writing a single word, the writer of a treatise bows to two teachers. Writing about the Dharma begins with humility.

quiz.q: Among the five marks of calm-abiding, which two are transcendent?
options: those of the root form and formless absorptions, the deepest and beyond the desire realm and so transcendent
those of approach concentration and the root form absorptions
those of the śrāvaka's and pratyekabuddha's engagement, and of the bodhisattva's
those of the exhaustive nature and of things as they are
quiz.why: The treatise calls the fourth and fifth transcendent, belonging to the engagement of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and of bodhisattvas. The first three, including the root absorptions, are explicitly mundane.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the outflow of ignorance from a mistaken wish for liberation?
options: any wish for liberation is itself craving, so every such wish is ignorance
the sensual craving of desire-realm beings
ignorance arising from a mistaken wish for liberation, rooted in clinging to a self
the residual habits of arhats
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this outflow is the affliction of ignorance produced by a mistaken wish for liberation, and the root error is clinging to a self, which is the fundamental ignorance giving rise to it.

quiz.q: This is rendered "producing latent tendencies through indeterminate objects." What is wrong?
options: nothing: 不定地 means objects neither good nor bad
it should be the form realm
隨眠 should be sleep
不定地 is the unconcentrated desire realm, not indeterminate objects
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 不定地 is the state without concentration, namely the desire realm, with its five kinds of sense objects. The English reads it as objects of uncertain character, which misses the term, as this concerns the outflow of desire.

quiz.q: Section 54 says form has five kinds but numbers only the elements and what is derived. What has happened?
options: the Chinese was rewritten; the treatise lists five, with the three of visibility and resistance as items
the treatise is written so, stating five and listing two, leaving the rest for thought
the English dropped three; the Chinese has all five
the five are form, sound, smell, taste, and touch
quiz.why: The treatise lists five items outright: the elements, the derived, and the three of visibility and resistance. The Chinese here takes the lecturer's paraphrase, turning five into two plus three, and the English follows it.

quiz.q: The fourth motive is rendered "what is too scattered may be condensed and what is too condensed may be expanded." What is the problem?
options: nothing: the treatise has both condensing and expanding, the English rendering them word for word
略 has been reversed
義 has been dropped
the treatise has only condensing what is scattered; the second half is added, from the lecturer's gloss
quiz.why: The treatise says only that scattered meanings are condensed. Master Cháng Bǎi adds an account of condensing and of expanding, which is his own development, and the English has absorbed it into the treatise's sentence.
